claims.explanation: Ryuvidine selectively kills cancer lines with mutations in FBXW7, which likely stabilizes pro-apoptotic substrates or enhances sensitivity to epigenetic inhibition, and in BRAF, which may create dependence on KDM5A-mediated survival. Lines with EGFR mutations or wild-type FBXW7/BRAF are relatively protected, suggesting that FBXW7 and BRAF mutations are sensitizing while EGFR mutation is protective.

features.basis: Enriched in selectively killed lines; FBXW7 loss may stabilize pro-apoptotic substrates or enhance epigenetic inhibitor sensitivity.
Enriched in killed melanoma and colorectal lines; BRAF-mutant cells may depend on KDM5A for survival.
EGFR-mutant lines are overrepresented among least affected lines, suggesting EGFR signaling confers resistance.
Ryuvidine inhibits KDM5A; high expression may predict sensitivity (PMID 31289306).
Ryuvidine inhibits SETD8; high expression may predict sensitivity (PMID 25137013).
Ryuvidine inhibits CDK4; high expression may predict sensitivity (PMID 26418250).
Ryuvidine annotated to inhibit CDK2; high expression may predict sensitivity.
TP53 mutations are common in killed lines, but also in protected lines; weak evidence.
PTEN mutations appear in several killed lines but also in protected lines; weak evidence.
PIK3CA mutations appear in several killed lines but also in protected lines; weak evidence.
ARID1A mutations appear in some killed lines but also in protected lines; weak evidence.
KMT2D mutations appear in some killed lines but also in protected lines; weak evidence.
